written.myAnswer: ASCII assigns numeric codes to characters so computers can represent and process text.

ASCII uses 7 bits to represent 128 characters, mainly those used in English. Unicode provides code points for characters from writing systems around the world and can represent over a million characters.
Unicode maps graphic characters used in the world's writing systems to code points. Encoding forms such as UTF-8, UTF-16 and UTF-32 represent those code points in bytes.

Unicode assigns a code point to each character, and encoding forms such as UTF-8, UTF-16 and UTF-32 represent those code points in bytes. For example, Latin capital A is U+0041 and the Urdu letter ب is U+0628.
